title: Complete 8-bit digital-to-analog converter with input latch, reference and output amplifier

sources.document: Analog Devices AD558 DACPORT Low Cost Complete uP-Compatible 8-Bit DAC, in Analog Devices 1984 Data-Acquisition Databook Volume I (pages 9-35 to 9-42)

pins.name: CE
pins.text: chip enable, active low; latch is open while /CE and /CS are both low

pins.name: CS
pins.text: chip select, active low; same timing and function as /CE

pins.name: VCC
pins.voltage: +4.5 V to +16.5 V (+11.4 V min for the 10 V range)

pins.name: VOUTSELECT
pins.text: output range select: to VOUT for 0-2.56 V, to GND for 0-10 V (Figure 3)

functions.text: VOUT = code / 256 x full scale: 0-2.55 V on the 2.56 V range, 0-9.961 V on the 10 V range (code table page 9-38). The latch passes the data while /CE and /CS are both low and holds it from the rising edge of either (Table I, page 9-40).

state.changesOn: level: transparent while /CE and /CS are both low
rules: /CE low and /CS low: the latch follows DB0-DB7 (transparent)
/CE or /CS goes high: the data present at the rising edge is held
/CE or /CS high: previous data stays latched

electrical.notes: Digital inputs: logic 1 2.0 V min, logic 0 0.8 V max, 100 uA max input current. Output: source 5 mA; sink is a passive pull-down to ground (2 kohm on the 2.56 V range, 10 kohm on the 10 V range). Supply current 15 typ / 25 max mA. Settling to 1/2 LSB: 0.8 typ / 1.5 max us (2.56 V range), 2.0 / 3.0 us (10 V range) (page 9-36).

timingLimits.text: data set-up time tDS before the rising edge of /CE or /CS
data hold time tDH after the rising edge of /CE or /CS

notes: Pin names are the ones in Figure 1 (page 9-37); both pin 12 and pin 13 are labelled GND there, pin 13 is the analog ground (block diagram page 9-35).

behaviour.reason: the output is an analog voltage, which a logic formula cannot express; the input latch is described in state (AD558 data sheet, Analog Devices 1984 Data-Acquisition Databook Vol. I, page 9-40).
